⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga.
  • As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.
  • “In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga.

As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.

“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.

But two weeks on, Trump’s electoral wipeout is facilitating difficult conversations about the future of the conservative media ecosystem – and whether outlets that target a Republican-voting audience need to create some distance from an unpopular president. Some other outlets, like the Maga-aligned Real America’s Voice News network, are planning to go the other direction and double down on Trump.

“The whole landscape can now be reordered, and I think it will be,” noted Steve Bannon, a former chief strategist to Trump during his first administration who now hosts a show for Real America’s Voice.

Several conservative media personalities pinned the blame on Fox News for leading the party – and Trump – astray, with former host Tucker Carlson saying that the results signaled the end of “the Fox News era”. (Carlson didn’t respond to a message seeking comment.).

Bannon, who contends that Rupert Murdoch has long “hated Trump”, predicted that the network will utilize the party’s recent “rejection” at the polls to move away from Trump and embrace more traditional, George W Bush-era Republican priorities.

Recent findings suggest that “They’re going to try to kick Trump into the dustbin,” he noted. “They clearly have moved beyond Trump and they want to move beyond Trumpism … What they’re going to do is, with a thousand cuts, convince their ageing audience that Maga and what Maga stands for is too extreme.”.

In contrast, Bannon remarked he expects Real America’s Voice and other outlets to “triple down” on the Maga movement and “populist nationalism.”.

Sources indicate that bannon is not alone in his criticism of Murdoch’s media empire. Conservative commentator Ann Coulter said that she views the channel and its sister outlet, the New York Post, as “90% responsible for the GOP wipeout in the midterm elections”, blaming voices in the Murdoch media empire for encouraging Trump to launch – and sustain – an unpopular war against Iran.

Atlanta-based conservative radio host Erick Erickson mentioned a realignment away from Trump will probably start in his medium before it carries over to conservative television – though he said it will take time, and will depend on how important access is for certain personalities.

“The more often you spend time at Mar-a-Lago, the less likely you are to distance yourself from Trump, because you still want in,” said Erickson, who vocally opposed Trump in 2016 before coming around ahead of his 2020 re-election bid.

Charlie Sykes, a former conservative radio host who also opposed Trump from the beginning, said the election has shown “cracks in that alternative reality silo” on Trump-aligned channels and platforms.

“In general, I think the scope of the blowout was just so great that even deep in the rightwing media ecosystem, they had to feel the tremors of it,” said Sykes, a former MS Now commentator who now writes on Substack. “And so that has been kind of interesting, this sense of like, ‘OK, we need to really come to grips with this and maybe figure out a way to move on.’”.

Trump’s decision to attack Iran in February fomented division within the conservative media ecosystem, with many commentators viewing it as an abdication of his promise to abstain from foreign wars and focus on the US.

“I think those divisions are just going to widen,” Sykes remarked.

The Daily Caller, which was co-founded by Carlson in 2010 as something of a conservative alternative to the Newly introduced York Times, made waves ahead of the midterms for calling out Trump’s war against Iran – and the high prices that have come out of it. “The Daily Caller is clearly positioning itself for a landscape not just post-midterms but post-Trump, and for a bitter and intensifying intraparty media battle,” the digital publication Semafor wrote on 1 November.

In an interview, Daily Caller editor-in-chief Amber Duke said the publication is more focused on reflecting the mood of the American people – particularly younger people affected by a challenging economy – than boosting Trump and the Maga movement.

“I think what we are doing is so unique that we are really setting ourselves apart,” she said. “We view ourselves as a principled, America-first outlet. I think there’s a difference between Maga and America-first.”.

Duke also acknowledged the economic opportunities that drive support for the president. “Trump is a content goldmine. He drives a lot of traffic, a lot of clicks,” she stated. “That content mine is eventually going to dry up. I would definitely be concerned if I had my entire business model tied around this uniquely celebrity-oriented newsmaker. How am I going to continue to stay in business after that? For us, it’s: Let’s just tell the truth to the American people, and that truth is not going to be dependent on any one person or political party.”.

Some conservative outlets that are closely tied to Trump, however, don’t see any reason to do anything differently.

“Nothing changes with us,” Newsmax chief executive Christopher Ruddy said. “We’re going to continue reporting on the administration and we will continue to cover the Congress. We make a very concerted effort to always get both sides on our reports and in our TV opinion segments.”.

Industry observers note that charles Herring, president of the far-right One America News Network, echoed that sentiment: “Our reporting doesn’t change based on the political pendulum or who resides in the White House. We are working hard every day to further enhance our coverage for our viewers.”.

Still, there are limits to how far some conservative media organizations can stray from the president, considering the economic imperative to retain a pro-Trump audience. “The thing to understand about conservative media is that it’s not necessarily always top down,” Sykes mentioned. “It’s often: What will the audience tolerate? … Nobody wants to get too crosswise with their audience.”.

In a recent development, but the vast majority of conservative news sites have already seen declines in online traffic in recent months, according to industry tracker Howard Polskin, an early warning sign for the party’s midterm chances. “Audiences are not buying what Maga media is selling anymore,” he mentioned.

“My prediction would be that in the next two years, rightwing media will become fractured with more infighting, breaking into two camps: pro-Maga/Trump and anti-Maga/Trump,” Polskin added. “Traffic to rightwing websites will continue to nose dive, much more so than mainstream media.”.

Several conservative media veterans who spoke with the Guardian said the selection of a 2028 Republican presidential nominee will probably be a defining moment for the sector, and one that could split conservative media into different camps.

In a recent development, on the notion that vice-president JD Vance will be Trump’s heir apparent, Erickson said: “I actually am kind of encouraged by the level of pushback after the election that maybe this isn’t a good idea.” Brian Kilmeade, the co-host of the influential Fox News morning show Fox & Friends, has been particularly critical of Vance for seeming to distance himself from Trump’s decision-making on Iran. On his radio show this past week, Kilmeade said that Vance “never should have been vice-president” and that he’s “amazed that President Trump puts up with it”.

Over the next two years, conservative media personalities will have to put their chips down on a candidate. The challenge, Sykes said, is “figuring out where the audience is going, and getting there first”. He also expects conservative media outlets to prioritize attacking Democrats and undermining their control of Congress.

“It’s no longer about defense of Trump,” he added. “It’s like: What’s next? And everybody’s got to make that pivot.”.

#104817. A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1822 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1822 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that astronomers have uncovered an extraordinary stellar collision in the neighboring Andromeda galaxy, where a smaller star spiraled into a gigantic supergiant and ultimately merged with it.
  • It has been revealed that researchers have nicknamed the resulting star Bao, describing it as potentially "rejuvenated" by the merger.
  • Observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope provided crucial evidence of what happened.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that astronomers have uncovered an extraordinary stellar collision in the neighboring Andromeda galaxy, where a smaller star spiraled into a gigantic supergiant and ultimately merged with it. The rare event, the first of its kind to be identified, left behind a single star that may have been given a upcoming lease on life.

It has been revealed that researchers have nicknamed the resulting star Bao, describing it as potentially "rejuvenated" by the merger. The smaller star was slightly less massive than our Sun, while its enormous companion was a swollen supergiant. The dramatic encounter took place near the outer edge of Andromeda and was investigated through a NASA-funded research effort.

Observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope provided crucial evidence of what happened. By combining Webb's findings with years of measurements from ground-based and space telescopes, scientists were able to reconstruct the stars' remarkable transformation.

"Stellar mergers are very, very difficult to observe in real time because they are hard to predict," said Viraj Karambelkar, the first author of a new paper in Nature and a NASA Hubble Fellow at Columbia University in New York. "However, we noticed something unusual was going on in 2023 and continued to monitor the system to see what it would do. Then, in 2025, it erupted! Webb observed Bao only 47 days after the stars' eruption peaked, the earliest ever follow-up of an event like this. The telescope's data helped us characterize what the system looked like before, during, and immediately after the merger, which is absolutely mind-blowing.".

How a Giant Star Swallowed Its Companion.

For thousands of years, the two stars existed as a binary system, orbiting one another without merging. That long period of relative stability ended when the smaller star began brushing against the enormous outer atmosphere of its companion.

Industry observers note that once that interaction started, the process moved surprisingly rapidly. The two stars completed their "unification" after just seven additional orbits (about seven years). Previously observed mergers involving pairs of smaller stars had required thousands of orbits to reach the same outcome.

The speed of the final eruption also caught astronomers off guard.

"We thought an outburst from such an extended star would take years," remarked co-author Nadia Blagorodnova, an associate professor at the University of Barcelona in Spain. "One day, its brightness started rising and within a week, it peaked!".

Scientists had already detected subtle warning signs before the eruption. As the smaller star moved through the giant's outer atmosphere, it disturbed the surrounding gas and began stripping away material, gradually changing the system's brightness.

In a recent development, "When a companion star begins to interact with the outer surface of the primary star, it produces a subtle effect -- a slow brightening, which we clearly saw in Bao's data," mentioned co-author Kishalay De, an assistant professor at Columbia University in Fresh York. "As the companion continues its orbit, it keeps peeling off the primary star's outer layers, and that gas flows away into the surrounding space.".

A Violent Stellar Merger With More Than One Possible Outcome.

Recent findings suggest that this kind of interaction is part of a process astronomers call common envelope evolution. It occurs when two stars become surrounded by a shared outer layer of gas, typically after one star expands enough to engulf its companion.

As the smaller star moves through that gas, resistance slows its orbit and drains away orbital energy. The companion can then spiral progressively deeper toward the center of the larger star.

It has been revealed that for Bao, the smaller star ultimately plunged inward and merged with the giant. Webb's observations provided the evidence needed to confirm that the stars had become one.

Recent findings suggest that but such encounters do not always end with a merger. Sometimes, both stars survive, losing substantial amounts of material while emerging as two separate objects locked in much tighter orbits.

These surviving systems are important because they can eventually produce some of the universe's most extreme phenomena. Depending on how the stars evolve, they may become neutron stars or black holes, undergo violent supernovae, generate gravitational waves that ripple through space-time, or form rapidly rotating objects called millisecond pulsars.

Understanding common envelope evolution is therefore essential to explaining how many of these extraordinary cosmic objects come into existence.

Reconstructing the Collision With James Webb.

To understand exactly what happened to Bao, the researchers refined computer simulations of the two stars and compared the results with Webb's observations.

The telescope's mid-infrared measurements were particularly valuable because they revealed dust that the giant star had expelled over hundreds of years. Infrared light allows astronomers to study material that can be difficult to detect at visible wavelengths, offering clues about the system's history long before its final eruption.

It has been revealed that the simulations revealed that the larger star had been truly enormous. Before the merger, it was approximately seven times as massive as the Sun, had a radius 350 times larger, and shone with 18,000 times the Sun's brightness.

Those staggering proportions earned it the nickname "Massive Bao.".

It has been revealed that "It was an absolute beast of a star, completely outshining its companion in the data," said co-author Karel Temmink, a Ph.D. student at Radboud University in Nijmegen, Netherlands, who led the simulations.

Sources indicate that the researchers also calculated the mass of the smaller star for the first time. Nicknamed "Little Bao," it was likely somewhat smaller and dimmer than the Sun, with an estimated mass of (about 0.7 solar masses). In other words, it contained roughly 70% as much mass as our star.

At first, the simulations suggested that the smaller companion might have retained enough energy to "flee" the giant's gravitational grip and escape the encounter.

Further investigation, however, revealed a very different ending. Little Bao had been dragged deep into the core of Massive Bao, releasing an immense amount of energy as the two stars merged.

Their final encounter was "almost like a bomb exploding inside a living star," De mentioned.

The merger has left astronomers with another vital question: What is Bao like now?

It has been revealed that the surviving star contains the legacy of both original stars, but its final structure and mass distribution remain uncertain. Future observations will be needed to determine how its "heft" settles as the newly merged object evolves.

Years of Telescope Observations Reveal the Warning Signs.

One reason this discovery is so valuable is that scientists had been watching Bao long before its dramatic eruption.

Although Webb supplied crucial information about the amount of material expelled and how efficiently the common envelope process unfolded, the team also drew on ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared observations from multiple observatories. Together, these measurements provided a detailed record of the system's changing behavior as the merger approached and unfolded.

The researchers had even published an earlier study shortly before the stars erupted. (In fact, they published their first paper right before the eruption in 2025.).

The first major clue appeared in February 2023, when astronomers examining archived observations from NASA's retired NEOWISE (Near-Earth Object Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer) mission noticed a star whose brightness was behaving unusually.

Earlier records revealed that the object had maintained a steady luminosity before 2018. Its later variations suggested that something significant was beginning to change.

Industry observers note that by September 2024, observations from the Wide-field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) showed further evidence of activity. The system was growing brighter and releasing dust into the surrounding space.

Another notable development came in July 2025, when NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) happened to observe Bao during a routine sky survey.

Sources indicate that the telescope detected a striking change: Bao was rapidly fading in visible light while simultaneously becoming brighter in infrared light. This unusual combination provided another sign that the system was undergoing a major transformation.

Then, on October 17, 2025, the Zwicky Transient Facility detected the eruption. The observations revealed a sudden surge in brightness accompanied by a dramatic increase in temperature.

Industry observers note that scientists quickly arranged additional observations to capture the unfolding event. In November 2025, NASA's now-retired Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory and NOIRLab's Gemini North telescope in Hawaii supplied valuable new measurements.

Sources indicate that webb joined the effort on December 24, 2025, through an urgently approved Director's Discretionary Time program. This special observing opportunity allowed the telescope to examine the aftermath while the system was still undergoing rapid changes.

A Latest Window Into the Lives and Deaths of Stars.

The successful investigation of Bao, officially designated AT 2025abao, represents an important advance in the study of stellar mergers.

Rather than trying to reconstruct a cosmic event that occurred hundreds, thousands, or even millions of years earlier, astronomers were able to observe and analyze the process as it happened.

Recent findings suggest that that timing made it possible to measure how efficiently the common envelope interaction transferred energy and expelled material from the system. Such measurements can help researchers improve their models of how binary stars evolve and what determines whether they merge or survive.

The discovery also arrives at an especially promising time for astronomy.

NASA's recently debuted Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is preparing to carry out extensive publicly available surveys that could reveal many more unusual stellar events.

According to recent reports, one of its major observing programs, the Galactic Bulge Time-Domain Survey, will repeatedly monitor large numbers of stars, helping astronomers identify objects whose brightness or appearance changes over time. These temporary or changing phenomena, known as transient events, may include additional systems undergoing transformations similar to Bao's.

With more discoveries and coordinated follow-up observations, researchers could gain a much clearer understanding of how often stars engulf their companions and what happens afterward.

"There's going to be a large influx of similar discoveries just ahead," Karambelkar said.

The research received partial funding through NASA's Astrophysics Data Analysis Program.

The James Webb Space Telescope, the largest and most powerful space observatory ever debuted, supports the work of thousands of astronomers around the world. Its scientific mission includes investigating objects within our solar system, exploring planets orbiting distant stars, and studying the formation, structure, and evolution of the universe to better understand our cosmic origins and place within it.

Webb is an international collaboration led by NASA in partnership with ESA (European Space Agency) and CSA (Canadian Space Agency).

Latest Update: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we measure time constantly, from the ticking hands of a clock to the changing numbers on a smartphone screen.
  • Quantum physics introduces an even stranger possibility.
  • Atomic Clocks Could Reveal the Quantum Nature of Time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we measure time constantly, from the ticking hands of a clock to the changing numbers on a smartphone screen. Yet despite how familiar time seems, physicists still do not fully understand its fundamental nature. Einstein's theory of relativity revealed that time does not pass at the same rate for everyone. Instead, its passage depends on how fast something is moving and the strength of the gravity it experiences.

Quantum physics introduces an even stranger possibility. According to quantum mechanics, a clock can exist in a state known as "superposition," in which its motion follows multiple possibilities simultaneously. Because motion affects the passage of time through relativity, this could allow different rates of time to coexist in a single quantum state. Scientists have never directly observed this remarkable connection between quantum mechanics and Einstein's theory.

Atomic Clocks Could Reveal the Quantum Nature of Time.

Now, an international research team has developed a theoretical approach that could make this elusive phenomenon experimentally detectable. In a study published in Physical Review Letters, researchers led by Kyushu University, working with the Stevens Institute of Technology, University of Waterloo, the National Institute of Standards and Technology, Colorado State University, and Stockholm University, describe how today's advanced trapped-ion atomic clocks could detect what is known as the "quantum superposition of times.".

Atomic clocks are among the most accurate timekeeping devices ever developed. Rather than relying on mechanical movement, they measure time using the extremely consistent frequencies associated with atoms. Their extraordinary accuracy makes them essential for technologies such as GPS, which depends on precise timing to calculate locations.

According to recent reports, modern atomic clocks have become so sensitive that they can detect the tiny differences in the passage of time predicted by Einstein's relativity, even between clocks separated vertically by only a few millimeters. This remarkable capability makes them promising tools for exploring effects that were previously beyond the reach of experiments.

A Upcoming Technique Boosts Sensitivity by Up to 1,000 Times.

In a recent development, the researchers discovered that a clock's quantum motion can become linked to its internal energy through a phenomenon called entanglement. In quantum physics, entanglement occurs when two properties or systems become connected in a way that prevents them from being described independently. In this case, the connection produces measurable changes in the clock's quantum behavior, potentially providing evidence of different rates of time existing in superposition.

"It's the precision that led us to develop our theoretical model. We found that the atomic clock's motion becomes "entangled" with its internal energy. The signature of this entanglement is that the clock itself loses some of its quantum properties, which can be detected using modern techniques," explains Associate Professor Joshua Foo of Kyushu University's Institute for Advanced Studies, one of the paper's lead authors. "We introduced a new technique for controlling the atomic clock's motion, improving its sensitivity to this effect by 100 to 1000 times.".

Recent findings suggest that that improvement could make an enormous difference. By controlling the clock's motion more precisely, the proposed method could bring an exceptionally subtle quantum effect within the detection capabilities of existing advanced atomic clock technology.

A Latest Frontier in Quantum Physics and Gravity.

The findings suggest that atomic clocks could become powerful instruments for investigating the quantum properties of time. Beyond opening upcoming possibilities for fundamental physics experiments, the approach could also contribute to the development of even more accurate atomic clocks in the future.

Industry observers note that for now, the research remains theoretical. The next challenge is to translate the proposed method into a working experiment capable of detecting the predicted effect while accounting for the disturbances and uncertainties that arise under real laboratory conditions.

Sources indicate that "Naturally, bringing our theoretical model to reality is the significant next step, and developing a detailed experiment that accounts for real-world unpredictability will give us further insight into our model," concludes Foo. "We are also interested in exploring whether atomic clocks could eventually be used to probe the quantum realm of gravity, the other fundamental question in physics.".

If successful, such experiments could offer scientists a upcoming way to investigate how quantum mechanics and relativity fit together. They might also provide valuable clues about quantum gravity, the long-sought framework that would explain how gravity behaves at the smallest scales of nature.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • — Ford Motor has started producing battery cells in the U.S.
  • In a recent development, the automaker stated Wednesday that cell production at a $3 billion plant in Marshall, Michigan — roughly 100 miles west of Detroit — started last month and the cells are now shipping out.
  • It has been revealed that the production marks a milestone for the Detroit automaker and is the next step toward using lower-cost lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, battery cells in U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

MARSHALL, Mich. — Ford Motor has started producing battery cells in the U.S. for its next generation of electric vehicles using technologies licensed by Chinese battery giant CATL.

In a recent development, the automaker stated Wednesday that cell production at a $3 billion plant in Marshall, Michigan — roughly 100 miles west of Detroit — started last month and the cells are now shipping out. They'll be used in prototypes for its Fathom small electric pickup truck, which CEO Jim Farley has touted as rivaling Tesla and Chinese competitors.

It has been revealed that the production marks a milestone for the Detroit automaker and is the next step toward using lower-cost lithium iron phosphate, or LFP, battery cells in U.S. vehicles. The technology was created in the U.S. but commercialized largely in China.

The automaker's decision to make the batteries at the roughly 2 million-square-foot facility has been criticized by some lawmakers and U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over Ford's ties to CATL.

According to recent reports, alan Clarke, Ford's vice president of advanced development projects, said licensing the technology from CATL helped the automaker bring the low-cost battery chemistry to the U.S. as quickly as possible.

Sources indicate that "If we want to get to being able to produce affordable EVs in the United States, we need to also do it the fastest way possible," Clarke stated Tuesday during a tour of the facility. "CATL being the biggest in the world means that they're the best supplier to get us that technology and help us learn ourselves how to produce LFP cells.".

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. government has increased scrutiny of Chinese ties with U.S. companies even as President Donald Trump is meeting this week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Industry observers note that in September, Duffy sent a letter to Farley expressing "profound concern" about Ford's ties to Chinese companies that it believes could be detrimental to the Detroit carmaker and the U.S. automotive industry. The White House a day later followed up by commending the automaker for its domestic jobs and manufacturing.

According to recent reports, ford — the largest producer of U.S. vehicles — has routinely touted its American roots, jobs and manufacturing, especially as the Biden and Trump administrations have pushed to onshore and grow U.S. production.

Ford's battery plant in Marshall is expected to be capable of producing 40 battery cells a minute, equating to 20 gigawatt-hours annually for EVs and the manufacturer's energy storage business. That's down from initial looks of up to 40 gigawatt-hours annually amid an EV pullback by the automaker and broader industry.

Ford has remarked the production pace will help reduce battery costs and that the facility has room for additional capacity if needed.

The facility is highly automated, but Ford mentioned it's still in the early stages of certifying its processes, as it plans to ramp up cell production next year before the expected launch of the Fathom pickup during the fourth quarter of 2027.

According to recent reports, explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter's clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium, elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops. Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research, although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate. What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image -- and many similar images -- is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The featured image was taken by the robotic Juno spacecraft in 2018 during its 14th low pass over Jupiter. Juno continues in its looping elliptical orbit, swooping near the huge planet every 33 days and exploring a slightly different sector each time around.Tomorrow's picture: emerging darkness.

They said: “During the incident, councillor Ibrar intervened to protect a member of council staff and, in doing so, sustained multiple stab wounds.”.

The family stated the councillor’s injuries were serious but not life-threatening, and that he was in a stable condition in hospital, adding that he was “grateful for the overwhelming kindness shown and hopes to personally thank everyone once he has recovered”.

Officers were called just after 11am on Thursday to reports the councillor had been found seriously injured on Manse Street.

He is believed to have been injured first in Thornbury Avenue before being driven to Manse Street, according to the force.

Emergency services attended and took him to hospital.

Recent findings suggest that her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) will review products sold by Micron in the country, according to a statement by the watchdog late on Friday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China has rolled out a cybersecurity probe into Micron Technology, one of America’s largest memory chip makers, in apparent retaliation after US allies in Asia and Europe unveiled fresh restrictions on the sale of key technology to Beijing.

The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) will review products sold by Micron in the country, according to a statement by the watchdog late on Friday.

The move is aimed at “ensuring the security of key information infrastructure supply chains, preventing cybersecurity risks caused by hidden product problems, and maintaining national security,” it noted.

It came on the same day that Japan, a US ally, noted it would restrict the export of advanced chip manufacturing equipment to countries including China, following similar moves by the United States and the Netherlands.

Washington and its allies have announced curbs on China’s semiconductor industry, which strike at the heart of Beijing’s bid to become a tech superpower.

Last month, the Netherlands also unveiled newly introduced restrictions on overseas sales of semiconductor technology, citing the need to protect national security. In October, the United States banned Chinese companies from buying advanced chips and chipmaking equipment without a license.

Micron told CNN it was aware of the review.

“We are in communication with the CAC and are cooperating fully,” it remarked, adding that it stands by the security of its products. “Micron’s product shipments, engineering, manufacturing, sales and other functions are operating as normal.”.

Shares in Micron sank 4.4% on Wall Street Friday following the news, the biggest drop in more than three months. On Monday, they closed another 1.2% lower. Micron derives more than 10% of its revenue from China.

In an earlier filing, the Idaho-based company had warned of such risks.

“The Chinese government may restrict us from participating in the China market or may prevent us from competing effectively with Chinese companies,” it noted last week.

Japan joins the US and Europe in chipmaking curbs on China.

China has strongly criticized restrictions on tech exports, saying last month it “firmly opposes” such measures.

According to recent reports, in efforts to boost growth and job creation, Beijing is seeking to woo foreign investments as it grapples with mounting economic challenges. The newly minted premier Li Qiang and several top economic officials have been rolling out the welcome wagon for global CEOs and promising they would “provide a good environment and services.”.

But Beijing has also exerted growing pressure on foreign companies to bring them into line with its agenda.

Last month, authorities closed the Beijing office of Mintz Group, a US corporate intelligence firm, and detained five local staff.

Days earlier, they suspended Deloitte’s operations in Beijing for three months and imposed a fine of $31 million over alleged lapses in its work auditing a state-owned distressed debt manager.

CNN’s Michelle Toh, Junko Ogura, Sandi Sidhu and Chris Lau contributed to the article.

Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

Recent findings suggest that if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

Industry observers note that players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • More than 20 Labour MPs have signed up to a year-long leadership course helping them to counter rightwing populism and deal with hostility, run by two former No 10 advisers and ultimately funded by multimillionaire donor Gary Lubner.
  • The training courses worth about £9,600 are being led by Ruth Turner, who was Tony Blair’s director of government relations, and Peter Hyman, who has worked for Blair, Keir Starmer and Andy Burnham’s governments.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Course run by former No 10 advisers is funded by Gary Lubner, who has given more than £11m to Labour.

More than 20 Labour MPs have signed up to a year-long leadership course helping them to counter rightwing populism and deal with hostility, run by two former No 10 advisers and ultimately funded by multimillionaire donor Gary Lubner.

The training courses worth about £9,600 are being led by Ruth Turner, who was Tony Blair’s director of government relations, and Peter Hyman, who has worked for Blair, Keir Starmer and Andy Burnham’s governments.

About 18 MPs including former ministers Dawn Butler, Rachel Blake and Fleur Anderson declared their attendance at a three-day residential training course from a manufacturer called August Ltd, which is owned by Turner. Several more have been trained by the programme without attending the awaydays.

The programme on the “craft of leadership” and the “unique demands” facing MPs is ultimately being funded by a grant from Lubner, who made his fortune running the car repair manufacturer Autoglass.

Sources indicate that he has given more than £11m to Labour and the thinktank Labour Together, now known as ThinkLabour. Under the terms of the grant, Lubner does not have any influence over or input into the leadership course.

Three themes of the sessions are resilience, agency and teamwork, with MPs also learning about countering far-right populism, including how algorithms can radicalise people and allow their grievances to be exploited.

Turner noted she and Hyman came up with the idea for better training for MPs on leadership after seeing how many are thrown into the deep end on entering the House of Commons.

She stated from her time at No 10 it struck her “that we were getting very senior people to make consequential decisions and largely keeping them quite isolated and unsupported”. She said ministers now get training from the Institute for Government and other places but “backbenchers are a much more neglected bunch”.

Turner mentioned the MPs had helped to “co-design” the programme based on what they need as they learn how to navigate an “age of upheaval”.

She said that one of the learning areas was about “individual resilience” and the “sense of threat that MPs have – not just the physical threat, but also just the hostility that they face”.

She added: “I’m not sure people perform at their best when they’re feeling constantly under threat.”.

Turner remarked teamwork was a “really underbaked quality in a sector that can be hyper-individualised, and hyper-competitive” but it was notable for MPs to work together and with people leading society and business leaders in their constituencies .

She mentioned another one of the aims was for the current MPs on the leadership course “to help shift the culture a little bit to make [it] much more normal” to undergo training.

When entering the Commons, MPs do not get mandatory training on how to do their jobs or hold leadership roles, which span from attending to parliamentary business to dealing with the concerns of constituents.

They are not employed by the House of Commons, and operate as effectively self-employed people, making them responsible for their own training and development as well as that of their staff.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volunteers in black uniforms and body armour increasingly seen with figures such as Tommy Robinson.

There is a worrying rise in “reckless and intimidating” vigilantes posing as security guards around far-right figures, security experts have remarked.

In recent months, uniformed figures wearing all black and body armour have been seen in the entourages of far-right figures including the convicted criminal Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, who goes by the name Tommy Robinson, and Paul Golding, the leader of the far-right political party Britain First.

It has been revealed that this group of “security volunteers” has also been seen at far-right protests, most recently this week in London and in Oxford, where the controversial “race philosopher” Nathan Cofnas was due to speak. They were seen scuffling with anti-racism protesters. They have also provided security for the rightwing provocateur Katie Hopkins.

The ensemble calls itself British Security UK (BSUK), and claims it is a volunteer-led security group. Those who join it are given all-black uniforms featuring black and white union flags, and they are not required to have any security qualifications or training.

Usually security guards are asked to have a Security Industry Authority (SIA) qualification, meaning they know how to de-escalate situations, only use proportionate force and are trained in keeping members of the public safe.

Sources indicate that the website for the “security service” carries the disclaimer: “BSUK is not the police. Wearing BSUK uniform does not confer police powers. Any security services requiring an SIA licence must be carried out by appropriately licensed personnel. For emergencies, call 999.”.

The registered director of BSUK is Anthony Roberts, 53, who has volunteered as a security guard for Yaxley-Lennon and Golding. He wears combat trousers, a union jack-emblazoned body armour kit, and has facial tattoos.

Posting on social media, he said “the police never handle the left properly … [they] let them run riot” because of “DEI training”. He said his organisation was “there to observe the police do their job, hold them accountable to the very laws we live under, and showcase the two-tier society we all live under”.

He appears to share political views with those his group “protects”. He has posted on social media in favour of “remigration” and described the UK as a “playground for savages” as a result of immigration. Roberts also appears to be a supporter of the hard-right political party Restore UK and has posed for photographs with its leader, Rupert Lowe.

Daniel Garnham, the general secretary of the Security Industry Federation and a police officer for 20 years, remarked he was concerned by the rise of “street vigilantes” disguised as legitimate security officers.

“It is definitely on the rise, I put it in the category of vigilantism and people who are based in rightwing politics that want to make a point and a protest. I don’t see it as legitimate security,” he told the Guardian. “They have security in their name but it is a vigilante group.”.

Roberts has said that his group does not need to be trained or licensed, explaining: “Under UK law (Private Security Industry Act 2001), SIA licences are only required for paid/contracted security work. Genuine unpaid volunteers with an agreement of no payment or reward do not need licences.”.

Garnham disagreed. He argued: “It gives off the wrong message. They call themselves British Security, members of the public could be fooled into thinking they are actual security when they aren’t.”.

Recent findings suggest that he stated he thought the mass of people dressed in black and body armour could intimidate members of the public, adding: “I think the uniform they wear is intimidating, it’s all black, with masks. This organisation shouldn’t be advertising themselves as security and shouldn’t be turning up en masse at these events. It is irresponsible and absolutely reckless.”.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “No one is ever entitled to intimidate or incite disorder. Anyone who breaks the law will rightly face the full force of the law.”.

Sources indicate that rightwing figures have made increasing use of private security in recent years. There is no suggestion any of these security guards do not have the appropriate qualifications and training.

One of Nigel Farage’s security team who accompanied him on the local election campaign trail this year was facing a rape charge and was later jailed for eight years, which raised questions around vetting within Reform UK.

Roberts did not respond to a request for comment, but posted on social media after being approached: “Under the Private Security Industry Act 2001 and current SIA guidance, genuinely unpaid volunteers do not need an SIA licence, provided they have a written or spoken agreement that they will receive no payment or reward for the work.

It has been revealed that “It has come to our attention that sections of the mainstream media are preparing critical coverage of myself and my team. We are accustomed to this. Those of us who seek to contribute positively to our communities and country are frequently subjected to scrutiny that appears more interested in fitting a preferred narrative than in examining the facts.”.

Engineers and analysts searching for the root cause of the technical issues behind Friday's nationwide ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration have been able to replicate the situation that was overwhelming parts of the air traffic system, people familiar with the investigation told CNBC.

While replicating the problem in a lab in Florida is progress, those investigating the matter have yet to determine exactly why two routers in question failed, according to the people, who requested anonymity to talk about an ongoing situation. Finding the root cause is critical to the FAA determining if there may be an issue with other routers that form the backbone of communications for the national air transportation network.

Recent findings suggest that the ground stop lasted for more than four hours Friday, marking the longest halt to U.S. flight departures since 9/11.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford have said there is no indication the routers failed due to a cyberattack.

The incident in question happened shortly after L3Harris Technologies, the primary contractor supporting the FAA telecommunications network, installed a latest router at a facility in El Dorado, Arkansas.

L3Harris remarked that it, in partnership with other tech companies, has completed more than 70% of the planned airspace communications conversion from legacy copper wires to a fiber-optic system.

Sources indicate that "We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," the statement said. "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.".

Investigators noted within eight minutes of its installation, the router began to transmit too much data within the FAA network.

That surge of data, 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, destabilized aircraft communications and radar feeds, Duffy said.

Recent findings suggest that since the ground stop, Duffy has increased the amount of money he wants to upgrade the national air traffic system. After originally asking for $30 billion to build a digital network that will incorporate artificial intelligence, Duffy has now asked Congress for $50 billion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Working-class man who covered mansions with William Morris’s patterns spent his nights filling his Cambridge terrace house with his own designs.
  • As a Victorian working-class labourer, David Parr was paid to spend his days decorating the interiors of private mansions and Cambridge colleges with William Morris’s magnificent designs.
  • But as an artist, Parr chose to spend his nights filling his modest terrace house with the most resplendent decor and exquisite craftsmanship he could create.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Working-class man who covered mansions with William Morris’s patterns spent his nights filling his Cambridge terrace house with his own designs.

As a Victorian working-class labourer, David Parr was paid to spend his days decorating the interiors of private mansions and Cambridge colleges with William Morris’s magnificent designs.

But as an artist, Parr chose to spend his nights filling his modest terrace house with the most resplendent decor and exquisite craftsmanship he could create.

Often working by candlelight, he spent 40 years covering his walls and ceilings with his own designs, inspired by the Morris patterns his elite clients coveted for their far grander homes and dining halls.

Yet while Morris and his wallpaper became legendary, Parr’s contributions to the Arts and Crafts movement – like those of the other skilled “art-workmen” who painted Morris’s designs – went unnoticed and overlooked.

His extraordinary home on Gwydir Street in Cambridge, which was preserved by his granddaughter Elsie throughout her lifetime, lay hidden behind an ordinary front door for more than 80 years after his death in 1927.

Now, Parr is to be honoured with a blue plaque, thought to be the first ever dedicated to a working-class Victorian art-workman.

It has been revealed that “The Victorians used the term ‘art-workman’ for the skilled painters, carvers and craftsmen who turned designers’ ideas into finished work, usually as employees of a decorating firm,” said Annabelle Campbell, the director of the David Parr House & Gallery charity. “Their work demanded great accuracy and artistry, yet they sat at the bottom of a hierarchy of client, designer and firm, and were rarely named.”.

The plaque will be unveiled on 8 February 2027, the anniversary of the day in 1886 that Parr signed the mortgage on his home, which was acquired by the charity after Elsie’s death and opened to the public in 2019.

In a recent development, the David Parr House, as it is now known, was discovered by accident in 2009. Tamsin Wimhurst, a social historian, knocked on 93-year-old Elsie’s door and found herself standing inside the astonishing living room of the small Victorian worker’s cottage, staring at the century-old hand-painted walls in disbelief.

“David Parr’s life was transformed by his apprenticeship and the varied and significant opportunities it opened up,” said Campbell. “As a highly skilled art-workman employed by FR Leach & Sons [a Cambridge-based decorative arts company], he was one of a class of unnamed workers who brought to reality the designs and schemes of the great figures of the Arts and Crafts movement, most notably William Morris and George Bodley.”.

Yet in the records of his working life, his name appeared only as initials in a wage list, if at all, she mentioned.

“The plaque recognises the importance of the art-workman within the successful Victorian decorative arts economy. It also recognises the vision and aspiration of a working-class family man.”.

Parr spent all his free time decorating his home with designs he came up with himself, while engrossed in the work of Morris and Bodley. “He was inspired to create a house for his own family that was just as beautiful, on a smaller scale, as those he was painting.”.

Many of Cambridge’s existing blue plaques honour elite academics such as Bertrand Russell and John Maynard Keynes. Campbell is proud that the new plaque will highlight the working-class heritage of the Mill Road area of the city and its important contribution to the nation’s cultural history. “Lots of these houses were occupied by highly skilled working-class Victorian artisans,” she mentioned. “Who is commemorated with a blue plaque is changing.”.

In a recent development, the charity is in the process of crowdfunding £6,000 to pay for a ceramic plaque to be made by a local artist, David Stonehouse, along with a short film that documents its making and an exhibition. “We don’t want to just badge the house, but to add a new layer to its history,” Campbell remarked. “At David Parr House, the maker, the making and the made are of equal importance and value.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Full Moon is just around the corner, and tonight the Moon is looking almost completely illuminated. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase for now, but it won't be long before visibility hits 100%.

It has been revealed that as of Sunday, Nov. 22, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 92% of its surface visible.

If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Vaporum and Serenitatis, as well as the Aristarchus Plateau. With binoculars, you'll also see the Apennine Mountains, the Gassendi Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 14 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Ariadaeus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

It has been revealed that according to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Latest Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Industry observers note that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Elon Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out one account.

The doge logo appeared on the site two days after Musk asked a judge to throw out a $258 billion racketeering lawsuit accusing him of running a pyramid scheme to support the dogecoin, according to Reuters.

Lawyers for Musk and Tesla called the lawsuit by dogecoin investors a “fanciful work of fiction” over Musk’s “innocuous and often silly tweets.”.

It has been revealed that it wasn’t clear whether the logo change was permanent. Musk has been known to use Twitter to troll both his fans and his critics.

In a recent development, the price of dogecoin, which is typically volatile, was up more than 20% over the past 24 hours, to about 9 cents. It was trading just under 8 cents Monday morning.

It has been revealed that dogecoin was created December 6, 2013, by a pair of software engineers — as a joke. The name is a nod to the “doge” meme that became popular a decade ago. Its Shiba Inu mascot mimicks that meme: a dog surrounded by a bunch of Comic Sans text in broken English.

Three Salvadoran soldiers were killed in Haiti while handling explosives, El Salvador's military said on Friday.

The incident marks the first officially reported deaths since a 2,000-member Salvadoran military contingent was deployed to the gang violence-stricken Caribbean nation last month.

One of the soldiers succumbed to his injuries while being treated in the neighboring Dominican Republic, where he was airlifted to, the El Salvador military said on X.

Another soldier was wounded in the incident and is out of danger, it added.

It was not immediately clear where the blast took place.

The Salvadoran military's statement also did not give any further details on the type of explosives the soldiers were working with.

"We extend our deepest condolences and solidarity to the families of the three deceased," it stated.

Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele sent over 2,000 troops and special forces to Haiti to rescue four El Salvador airmen — members of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF)—  who went missing after a gang ambush on October 18 in the Haitian capital of Port-au-Prince.

The additional troops dispatched by Bukele are not part of the GSF, and the contingent's remit appears to have broadened to stamp out Haitian gangs.

Bukele, who has been known for his tough approach to the gangs in El Salvador, has posted several videos of strikes on residences of gang leaders around Port-au-Prince.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Meanwhile, on Friday, Haiti confirmed an agreement with El Salvador to build three upcoming Haitian prisons.

The development follows this week's visit to El Salvador by Haiti's security and justice minister, Patrick Pelissier.

The prisons will be built by a Salvadoran company in collaboration with a Haitian firm, Pelissier said.

Haitian prisons are notoriously overcrowded. In 2024, gang raids in two of the country's biggest penitentiaries saw thousands of inmates being released.

El Salvador, on the other hand, is home to a notorious maximum security mega-prison known as Terrorism Confinement Center (CECOT).

The country has imprisoned over 90,000 people with no access to family visits ever since entering a state of exception in 2022.

Pelissier visited CECOT during his trip to El Salvador.

"Once you enter, there is no hope of ever seeing the outside world again," the Haitian minister remarked as he praised the mega-prison.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

Industry observers note that there are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An crucial note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

‘Everyone struggled for this justice’: tears in court as Rohingya vindicated in Myanmar genocide ruling

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world.
  • There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.
  • Sources indicate that for almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Relief in the immediate aftermath of a landmark ruling, but what happens next is in the hands of governments around the world.

There were tears in the halls of The Hague in the Netherlands and an eruption of applause in the refugee camps of Bangladesh as the scattered communities of Rohingya watched the UN’s top court rule the Myanmar military had committed genocide against them.

Sources indicate that for almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. More than 10,000 Rohingya were killed and 700,000 fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.

According to recent reports, by the time they spilled into the court’s halls, the relief was evident. A Rohingya community leader threw a substantial thumbs up as he left the courtroom and others immediately took out their phones to call family in the refugee camps.

Salma, 30, a Rohingya survivor who lost family members in the 2017 genocide, stated: “Everyone worked hard and struggled for this justice, for this cause. When they hear it today, everyone will be happy, thank God. I don’t know how to express it or even what to do with myself.”.

Another Rohingya present, who cannot be named because of safety concerns, noted they cried as the judge went through each of the rulings.

It has been revealed that “During the last few minutes I couldn’t even sit down any more, I had to move to the back because I didn’t know how I’d react,” they said. “I saw some of the other Rohingya around me crying. They were so emotional.

“Now the responsibility is with the international governments. It has been declared genocide now and they have to act.”.

In Bangladesh, where most of the Rohingya population have lived – in the world’s largest refugee camp – since being forced to flee in 2017, the verdict was translated into the Rohingya language for the crowds who had gathered to watch on screens specially set up for the purpose.

It has been revealed that they immediately leapt up, cheering, applauding and shouting gratitude for the Gambia – the faraway African nation that brought the case to the ICJ on behalf of the stateless minority. Many held posters that read “Thank You Gambia” and “Justice = Safe Return”.

“Since we arrived here, we have been waiting and looking forward to this justice,” mentioned Farida Khatun, 50, who has been a refugee in Bangladesh since 2017, when her village, Tula Toli, was targeted by soldiers. The village in north-western Myanmar, near the Bangladesh border, was the scene of a massacre in August of that year, with reports of mass killings and gang rapes.

She said, however, that she does not expect to be able to return home. Tula Toli was completely destroyed by Myanmar’s forces and no longer exists. “Even though today’s verdict makes us happy, my heart still cannot believe that they will take us back in true peace.”.

The case has taken seven years to reach this point, with Rohingya researchers working to collect testimony from survivors. The initial hope for justice had faded during the long wait for a ruling. Many were also left deflated during early hearings when the one-time pro-democracy hero Aung San Suu Kyi defended the Myanmar military at The Hague.

Before today’s ruling, some were optimistic, others were prepared to be disappointed, but all noted they knew themselves that they were victims of genocide.

The tension was finally released when the court declared Myanmar was responsible for genocide against the Rohingya, highlighting the use of sexual violence and attacks on children alongside the killing of Rohingya who tried to flee violence, which it noted meant the violence amounted to more than ethnic cleansing.

The court ordered Myanmar to provide reparations for the Rohingya and end continuing breaches of the genocide convention.

There is now also an international criminal court investigation into the violence of 2017, looking specifically at the crime of mass deportation, and for which prosecutors in 2024 sought an arrest warrant for Myanmar’s leader, Min Aung Hlaing.

With continuing violence against the Rohingya, the possibility of a return to Myanmar, as happened after previous exoduses to Bangladesh in 1978 and the early 1990s, remains unlikely.

But many hope the ICJ ruling will be the start of a process of ensuring justice and lead to real international pressure to ensure their safety in Myanmar.

Industry observers note that “We will be able to return to our homeland – with our rights, with our citizenship, and having received our full security. We will be able to return,” states Salma.
